messages.author: 2a780f5be56f33ab
messages.subject: "multi-method" model using eDNAoccupancy
parts:
Hi,
I am hoping someone can help me. I have eDNA and visual survey data from 12 sites with 4 sample locations per site (so 48 total locations). Each location was visited twice, approximately a month apart, over which time the animal's abundance (and therefore detection probability) at the sites likely increased.

I'm interested in comparing detection probability between the two methods. It seems like a "multi-method, multi-season" approach is warranted, treating the two survey rounds as "seasons".  Does this sound reasonable?

Also, I wish to include information about PCR-based detection of DNA in each lab ("technical") replicate, so the eDNAoccupancy package is attractive. Can anyone point me to code illustrating how to implement such a multi-method approach in this package?

Thanks,
Mike

messages.author: 7ac258fb6a0ab492
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] "multi-method" model using eDNAoccupancy
parts:
Dear Mike,
I'm not super familiar with the eDNAoccupancy package, but believe that it might only allow for single season estimation. 

There is a multiseason implementation of the multi-method model. It is developed here: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ece3.4822, and the authors include JAGS code. This multiseason version is also available in Program MARK.

The mutliseason model comes at a cost of estimating additional parameters. Your sample size of 12 sites is on the small size, so it might be better to run two single season models and to make comparisons between them.

Best,
Brittany
